Canopy biodiversity studies in Sinharaja UNESCO World Heritage Forest Reserve.

# Rainforest Survey — Sinharaja Forest Reserve

Sinharaja is Sri Lanka's last viable area of primary tropical rainforest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Our team conducts regular canopy and understorey surveys to monitor species composition, abundance, and seasonal variation across different forest strata.

## Methodology

We use a combination of point-count transects for birds, pitfall traps for herpetofauna, and botanical quadrats for vegetation assessment. Camera traps placed along wildlife trails provide continuous data on mammal activity.

## Key Findings

Our surveys have recorded over 60 endemic bird species within the reserve, as well as numerous amphibians and reptiles unique to the Sri Lankan wet zone. Continued monitoring reveals long-term trends in population dynamics linked to rainfall patterns and forest fragmentation at the reserve margins.

Mapping safe wildlife corridors for Asian elephants across central Sri Lanka.

# Elephant Corridors — Central Sri Lanka

Sri Lanka has one of the highest densities of Asian elephants in the world. As agricultural land expands, elephant populations face increasing fragmentation of their traditional ranging areas, leading to human–elephant conflict. Our corridor mapping project identifies and prioritises habitat linkages that allow elephants to move safely between protected areas.

## Methodology

We combine GPS collar data from radio-tracked individuals, satellite land-cover analysis, and field surveys of vegetation quality and water availability to model optimal corridor routes. Community interviews document conflict hotspots and traditional elephant movement knowledge.

## Conservation Impact

Corridor maps produced by our team have been submitted to the Department of Wildlife Conservation to inform the National Elephant Conservation Action Plan, helping to reduce both elephant mortality and crop damage in border communities.

Health assessments and species mapping of Sri Lanka's coral reef systems.

# Coral Reef Monitoring — Sri Lanka's Coastal Waters

Sri Lanka's coastal waters support diverse coral reef ecosystems that are vital for fisheries, coastal protection, and marine biodiversity. Rising sea temperatures, pollution, and destructive fishing practices threaten these habitats. Our reef monitoring programme tracks coral cover, bleaching events, and fish community composition at sentinel sites around the island.

## Methodology

Trained dive teams conduct Belt Transect surveys following the Reef Check protocol. Benthic composition is recorded using point-intercept transects, while fish diversity is assessed using underwater visual census methods. Water quality parameters including temperature and pH are logged continuously at moored sensors.

## Recent Results

Bleaching events following the 2023 thermal anomaly affected up to 40% of live coral cover at shallow reef sites on the north-west coast. Recovery monitoring is ongoing, with hard coral recruits now visible at most affected sites.

Documenting migratory and endemic bird species in Sri Lanka's northern wetlands.

# Wetland Birds — Northern Lagoons and Tanks

The shallow lagoons, estuaries, and ancient irrigation reservoirs (tanks) of northern Sri Lanka provide critical staging and wintering habitat for thousands of migratory waterbirds on the Central Asian Flyway. Our wetland bird surveys document species diversity, population counts, and habitat quality across key sites.

## Methodology

Systematic counts are conducted at fixed watch points during peak migration (October–December) and again during the breeding season (March–May). Breeding colonies are mapped using drone photography, and ring-resighting data contribute to international wader monitoring networks.

## Highlights

Our counts have confirmed internationally significant concentrations of Lesser Sand Plover, Black-tailed Godwit, and Painted Stork at several tank systems. We have also documented breeding records for three globally threatened species at sites not previously known to hold nesting populations.

Cataloguing Sri Lanka's unique flowering plant species and their habitats.

# Endemic Flora — Sri Lanka's Plant Heritage

Sri Lanka harbours approximately 3,200 flowering plant species, of which nearly 900 are endemic — found nowhere else in the world. Many of these species exist in highly restricted habitats and are threatened by deforestation, invasive plants, and climate change. Our flora documentation project builds a comprehensive photographic and herbarium record of endemic species across all habitat types.

## Methodology

Field botanists conduct survey transects in understudied forest patches, montane grasslands, and stream margins. Voucher specimens are deposited at the National Herbarium in Peradeniya. Geo-referenced photographic records are contributed to the iNaturalist Sri Lanka flora project, creating a publicly accessible citizen-science dataset.

## Significance

Our surveys have documented several species in new locations, extending known ranges, and have recorded at least four populations of Critically Endangered species that had not been observed in the wild for over a decade.

Population monitoring of the iconic Sri Lankan Leopard in Yala and beyond.

# Leopard Studies — Sri Lankan Leopard Population Monitoring

The Sri Lankan Leopard (*Panthera pardus kotiya*) is an endemic subspecies and the apex predator of the island's ecosystems. With an estimated wild population of fewer than 1,000 individuals, the subspecies faces pressure from habitat loss, human–wildlife conflict, and road mortality. Our camera-trap network provides systematic population estimates and monitors individual home ranges and behaviour.

## Methodology

A grid of 60 camera trap stations is maintained across Yala National Park and buffer zones. Individual leopards are identified by unique rosette patterns. Mark-recapture modelling (spatial capture-recapture) generates density and abundance estimates. Mortality records and conflict incidents are collected through a network of trained community reporters.

## Outcomes

Our population estimates feed directly into the Sri Lanka Leopard Conservation Action Plan. Community education programmes developed from conflict data have reduced retaliatory killings in three buffer-zone villages over the past two years.

#### Inline

Inline link format like this: `[Link Text](URL "Title")`

#### Reference

You could predefine link references. Format like this: `[id]: URL "Title"`

Title is also optional. And the you refer the link, format like this: `[Link Text][id]`

Code:

    [id]: http://example.com/  "Optional Title Here"
    This is [an example][id] reference-style link.

This is [an example][id] reference-style link.

That is:

- Square brackets containing the link identifier (**not case sensitive**, optionally indented from the left margin using up to three spaces);
- followed by a colon;
- followed by one or more spaces (or tabs);
- followed by the URL for the link;
- The link URL may, optionally, be surrounded by angle brackets.
- optionally followed by a title attribute for the link, enclosed in double or single quotes, or enclosed in parentheses.

The following three link definitions are equivalent:

Code:

    [foo]: http://example.com/  "Optional Title Here"
    [foo]: http://example.com/  'Optional Title Here'
    [foo]: http://example.com/  (Optional Title Here)
    [foo]:   "Optional Title Here"

# Biodiversity Assessment

Beyond simply listing species, a full biodiversity assessment evaluates the functional health of ecosystems — the interactions between species, the integrity of food webs, and the long-term viability of populations. Serendib Eco Lab offers comprehensive biodiversity assessments that go beyond checklists to deliver ecologically meaningful results.

As part of our commitment to sharing Sri Lanka’s natural wonders, we integrate wildlife photography into our fieldwork and offer opportunities for participants to join our research trips and tours. Capture rare species and unique habitats alongside our scientists, and gain hands-on experience in ecological research.

**Booking is available** for guided biodiversity assessment tours and research expeditions. Contact us or visit our booking page to reserve your spot.

## What We Assess

- **Species richness and endemism**: Identifying rare, endemic, and threatened species using IUCN criteria
- **Population viability**: Estimating population sizes and modelling long-term persistence
- **Habitat quality**: Assessing vegetation structure, connectivity, and disturbance history
- **Ecosystem services**: Quantifying pollination, water regulation, and carbon storage values

## Deliverables

Clients receive a detailed report including species lists with conservation status, habitat maps, population estimates, threat assessments, and management recommendations aligned with national and international biodiversity frameworks.

# Community Education & Outreach

Conservation that is not rooted in local communities is rarely sustainable. Serendib Eco Lab runs a range of education and outreach programmes designed to build environmental awareness, practical conservation skills, and long-term stewardship among communities living alongside Sri Lanka's wildlife.

We also offer unique opportunities for local communities and visitors to participate in wildlife photography workshops, guided tours, and research trips. These experiences foster a deeper appreciation for Sri Lanka’s biodiversity and empower participants to become ambassadors for conservation.

**Booking is available** for our photography workshops, tours, and research expeditions—contact us or visit our booking page to join an upcoming event.

## Programmes

- **School environmental clubs**: Hands-on nature education for primary and secondary students in rural areas
- **Community wildlife monitor training**: Teaching residents to record and report wildlife sightings, conflict incidents, and habitat changes
- **Village nature trails**: Developing guided trail infrastructure that generates eco-tourism income while incentivising habitat protection
- **Farmers and wildlife workshops**: Helping agricultural communities adopt practices that reduce human–wildlife conflict
- **Citizen science campaigns**: Seasonal bioblitzes that generate biodiversity data while engaging the public

## Our Reach

Our education programmes have reached over 4,000 schoolchildren and 800 community members across 15 villages in the wet zone and dry zone of Sri Lanka.

# Conservation Planning

Effective conservation requires more than field data — it requires strategic thinking about where to act, what to protect, and how to allocate limited resources. Serendib Eco Lab brings together biodiversity data, spatial analysis, and stakeholder knowledge to develop conservation plans that are both scientifically robust and practically achievable.

We also believe in engaging the public and nature enthusiasts through immersive experiences. Our conservation planning work is complemented by wildlife photography tours, guided nature expeditions, and research trips that allow participants to witness conservation in action and contribute to real-world projects.

**Booking is available** for our tours and research expeditions—contact us or visit our booking page to join an upcoming conservation experience.

## Our Approach

We use systematic conservation planning tools, including Marxan and Zonation, to identify priority areas for protection and management. Plans are co-developed with communities, government agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure local ownership and long-term implementation.

## Planning Products

- **Species recovery plans** for threatened endemic taxa
- **Protected area management plans** aligned with IUCN green list standards
- **Wildlife corridor strategies** linking fragmented habitat patches
- **Land-use zoning recommendations** for buffer zones and multiple-use landscapes
- **Restoration priority maps** for degraded ecosystems

# Ecological Field Surveys

Our field survey teams operate across all of Sri Lanka's major ecosystem types — tropical rainforest, dry-zone scrubland, montane cloud forest, freshwater wetlands, and coastal habitats. We design and execute biodiversity surveys that provide rigorous, quantitative data on species composition, abundance, and habitat condition.

We invite nature enthusiasts, photographers, and aspiring researchers to join our ecological field surveys through guided tours and research trips. Experience the thrill of wildlife photography in the field, learn scientific survey techniques, and contribute to real conservation work.

**Booking is available** for our field survey tours and expeditions. Contact us or visit our booking page to secure your place.

## Survey Types

- **Vegetation surveys**: Quadrat and transect-based assessments of plant community structure and composition
- **Bird surveys**: Point-count and mist-netting methodologies following international standards
- **Herpetological surveys**: Visual encounter surveys, pitfall arrays, and acoustic monitoring for frogs
- **Mammal surveys**: Camera-trap grids and track-station arrays

# About Serendib Eco Lab

Serendib Eco Lab is an ecological research organisation based in Sri Lanka, dedicated to the scientific study, conservation, and celebration of the island's remarkable natural heritage. "Serendib" — the ancient Arabic name for Sri Lanka — reflects our deep connection to this extraordinary land and its biodiversity.

We are passionate about sharing Sri Lanka’s wild beauty with the world through immersive wildlife photography, guided tours, and hands-on research expeditions. Whether you are a photographer, nature lover, or aspiring researcher, our experiences are designed to inspire, educate, and connect you with the wonders of Sri Lanka’s ecosystems.

## Our Mission

We exist to advance the scientific understanding of Sri Lanka's ecosystems and to translate that knowledge into meaningful conservation action. Through rigorous field research, community engagement, and evidence-based advocacy, we work to protect the species and habitats that make Sri Lanka one of the world's most important biodiversity hotspots.

## What We Do

Sri Lanka is home to an exceptional diversity of life. As an island that has been geographically isolated for millions of years, it has evolved a remarkable array of endemic species — plants and animals found nowhere else on Earth. Our work spans the full breadth of the island's ecosystems:

- **Wildlife Photography Tours** — Join our expert guides and photographers on unforgettable journeys to capture Sri Lanka’s most iconic and elusive wildlife in their natural habitats.
- **Guided Nature Tours & Research Trips** — Participate in field expeditions that blend adventure, education, and conservation, suitable for all experience levels.
- **Booking Available** — Secure your spot on our upcoming tours and research trips directly through our website or by contacting us.

We also conduct:

- **Tropical rainforests** — surveying the rich canopy life of Sinharaja and the Knuckles Range
- **Wetlands and waterways** — monitoring aquatic biodiversity and migratory waterbirds
- **Coastal and marine habitats** — assessing coral reef health and beach-nesting turtle populations
- **Dry zone scrublands** — documenting reptiles, invertebrates, and endemic dry-zone flora

## Our Research Approach

Every project we undertake is grounded in sound scientific methodology. We conduct systematic species surveys, long-term population monitoring, habitat mapping using GIS technology, and environmental DNA sampling. Our data is published in peer-reviewed journals and made available to conservation managers, policymakers, and the public.

## Community & Education

We believe that lasting conservation begins with local communities. We run environmental education programmes in schools, train community wildlife monitors, and partner with village communities to develop sustainable land-use practices that benefit both people and nature.

## Get Involved

Whether you are a researcher, a student, a nature enthusiast, or an organisation looking to assess environmental impact, we welcome collaboration. If you’re interested in joining a wildlife photography tour, participating in a research expedition, or booking a custom experience, contact us at **info@serendibecolab.com** or visit our booking page to learn more and reserve your place.
